sources.attribution: Saikr competition registration/listing platform; MathorCup official site links its registration entry point to Saikr, but this search page is not the committee's rule document.
directly_supported: Search result shows one 2026 seventh Big Data listing with registration 2026-08-13 to 2026-10-23 and competition 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-30.
The same search result also shows a second listing of the same named competition with registration 2026-05-27 to 2026-10-19 and a single competition date 2026-11-14.
inference: October 23-30 is a plausible schedule for the user's October competition, while October 23 may also be registration close; the duplicate inconsistent entries mean the schedule should be confirmed against the actual official PDF/platform entry before reliance.
sources.limits: Conflicting duplicate listings; not sufficient by itself to settle official dates, stages, or deadlines.

sources.published: Charter revision dated 2025-08; PDF is a 2025 sixth-edition registration notice plus charter
sources.attribution: China Society of Optimization, Overall Planning and Economic Mathematics / MathorCup Big Data competition committee; hosted on official MathorCup files domain
directly_supported: The contest is a separate Big Data event; it uses initial and semifinal rounds, with the top 10% advancing in the 2025 rules.
The 2025 charter requires an answer in paper form and, if programming is used, source code and explanatory material; one submission per team per day.
The 2025 evaluation criteria include paper quality, completeness/correctness/efficiency of code, answer quality on test data using task-relevant measures, and innovation.
The 2025 rules prohibit plagiarism and require citation of public sources.
inference: These are useful possible workflow requirements to check, but must not be carried forward as 2026 requirements without the 2026 charter.
sources.availability: Full official PDF text publicly accessible through web extraction.
sources.limits: Prior edition only; it is not evidence of 2026 dates, rules, evaluation, data access, or AI policy. It does not mention generative AI in the extracted charter. Silence is not permission.

sources.attribution: MathorCup official site; notice signed MathorCup committee in notice index
directly_supported: Regular 16th-edition contest ran 2026-04-17 08:00 through 2026-04-21 09:00, with five problems and group-dependent choices.
The official notice index correction says D-problem task quantities were multiplied by ten and wording/objective were corrected; the new D ZIP is linked.
inference: A workflow should preserve the corrected D version as authoritative for that regular contest rather than analyzing an earlier downloaded copy.
sources.availability: Official contest release HTML and official correction notice accessible.
sources.limits: This is the April regular MathorCup competition, not the later Big Data competition. The page directs users to check the Saikr registration site for updates.

sources.published: University repost on notice page dated 2026-04-10; not itself the committee's canonical charter
sources.attribution: Notice reproduced from Linyi University Math/Statistics student association; listed on official MathorCup site as information
directly_supported: The April regular competition notice says teams may use books, computers, software, and browse the internet; advisers may not guide or discuss during the contest; teams must submit by the stated deadline.
inference: This general wording does not explicitly establish whether generative AI is allowed or what disclosure is required.
sources.availability: HTML content accessible on official MathorCup notice index.
sources.limits: Secondary university notice rather than a dedicated AI rule. Do not generalize this provision to the Big Data competition.

sources.attribution: Official CUMCM English site; organizer CSIAM (China Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics)
directly_supported: AI includes LLMs, generative AI, code-assistance tools, and AI agents; use is permitted as assistance subject to openness/transparency, team-led core modeling and analysis, and manual review/verification.

Paper must contain a prescribed AI usage declaration; use requires a PDF supporting-material file named 'Details of AI Tool Usage.pdf' describing tools/models, purpose/stages, prompting/process, and adoption/modification/verification of outputs (except language polishing).
Concealment, false declaration, or submitting AI-generated core analysis without required human review can revoke award eligibility; inconsistent prior provisions are superseded from 2026-09-01.
inference: This is a binding distinction for CUMCM 2026, not a MathorCup policy; it cannot be imported into MathorCup Big Data rules.
sources.availability: Official HTML and downloadable DOCX attachment accessible.
sources.limits: Applies to CUMCM only. A workflow that replaces the contestant team's core modeling with autonomous agent output would conflict with the stated team-led requirement.

sources.attribution: National CUMCM Organizing Committee; official mcm.edu.cn PDF
directly_supported: Advisers may not guide teams during the contest; teams must solve independently and may not communicate about problems with outsiders or browse/post/discuss them on discussion platforms; AI assistance is allowed only under the separate AI-use provisions, with teams fully responsible for originality, authenticity, and accuracy.
sources.limits: CUMCM-specific. Do not confuse its ban on outside-human discussion with the separate rule permitting declared, manually checked AI assistance.

sources.published: Listed sample papers dated 2003, 2009, and 2011; page current when accessed 2026-10-07
sources.attribution: Official CUMCM site, organized by CSIAM
directly_supported: The official English site exposes sample solution papers for CUMCM-2003, 2009, and 2011 problems.
inference: These can be used to inspect historical paper organization and explanatory style, not to establish current contest scoring or a guaranteed winning template.
sources.availability: Public sample paper list with per-paper links.
sources.limits: Small, old selection; no verified raw data/code or current evaluation rubric on this page. These are sample solutions, not evidence that their methods are uniquely correct or award-winning.

sources.attribution: Roberts et al., peer-reviewed Ecography article; DOI 10.1111/ecog.02881; public author/institution-hosted PDF also located at https://www.wsl.ch/lud/biodiversity_events/papers/Roberts_et_al-2017-Ecography.pdf
directly_supported: The paper studies validation for temporal, spatial, hierarchical, and phylogenetic dependence and explains that ordinary random folds can mislead when data are structured; it discusses blocked approaches and non-causal predictors as overfitting/leakage risks.
inference: For time-ordered or grouped Big Data tasks, choose validation splits that mimic the intended deployment/generalization target and keep related records from crossing train/test boundaries when appropriate.
sources.availability: Public PDF located at an institutional host; DOI landing page is the canonical citation.
sources.limits: Methodological guidance, not a competition rule; the correct split depends on the task and data-generating structure. Article is not a ready-made score threshold/template.

inference: It is a reasonable provenance example for concise, routed, referenced procedures and explicit validation steps, but its SDK-specific workflow does not establish a modeling competition workflow.

sources.limits: Not competition guidance or modeling evaluation evidence; currentness of each referenced SDK capability must be rechecked.

inference: Do not use its old skills catalog as a current prescription without checking the newer official repository.
sources.limits: Repository remains public and historical materials can inform structure; its deprecated status makes it stale as current installation advice.
